newTitle: Office 2024 vs Microsoft 365: Which Is Better for Business?
newExcerpt: Office LTSC 2024, Home & Business 2024 or Microsoft 365? Compare licensing, cost over time and the right choice for Indian businesses.
appendBody:
## The three Office products side by side

Buyers often meet three different things under the name "Office" and treat them as variants of one product. They are not.

| | Office LTSC Professional Plus 2024 | Office Home & Business 2024 | Microsoft 365 Business Standard |
|---|---|---|---|
| Price excluding GST | {{price:microsoft-office-ltsc-professional-plus-2024}} one time, per device | {{price:microsoft-office-home-and-business-2024}} one time, per device | {{price:microsoft-365-business-standard}} per user per year |
| Licensed to | A device, under volume licensing | A single PC or Mac | A named user |
| Applications | Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, Publisher, Access | Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook | Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, plus web and mobile versions |
| Business email, Teams, 1 TB OneDrive | No | No | Yes |
| Feature updates | None | None | Continuous |
| Volume activation (KMS or MAK) | Yes | No | Not applicable |

Each column answers a different question: licensing fixed machines in bulk, giving a few people desktop Office without a subscription, or running mail, files, meetings and applications for a team.

## Home & Business 2024: the middle option people overlook

If the choice is between LTSC and Microsoft 365, the third product is easy to forget. Office Home & Business 2024 is a one-time purchase for one PC or Mac, with Outlook included and no renewal. It does not support volume activation and carries no email hosting, OneDrive or Teams.

It fits a very small business, say a three-person consultancy, where each person already has a hosting arrangement for mail and nobody needs shared storage. It does not fit anyone who wants central assignment and control of licences, because it is bought machine by machine.

The cost trap is the same as with LTSC. If you also need business email on your own domain, the subscription route usually works out better once you add the mail hosting you would otherwise buy separately. Price the whole bundle of needs, not only the applications.

## A fair way to compare cost

Do not compare one number against another. Build the comparison for your own estate in five steps.

1. **List the devices and the people.** A perpetual licence follows the device, a subscription follows the person. Fifty laptops used by fifty people look similar either way, but fifty people with seventy devices do not.
2. **List what you would buy anyway.** Mail hosting, file storage, meeting software, a backup of shared files, and mobile access. Put each on the perpetual side if the subscription includes it.
3. **Set a realistic horizon.** Hardware refresh cycles in Indian offices are often four to five years. Compare over that period, not over one year.
4. **Add the replacement event.** A perpetual licence is replaced by a project at the end of its supported life. A subscription is replaced by nothing, because it updates. Count the labour of the project.
5. **Check the accounting treatment.** A perpetual licence is a capital item and a subscription is an operating expense. Which suits you depends on your finance team and tax position, so ask your accountant rather than assuming. For the input credit side, see [GST input credit on software purchases](/blog/gst-input-credit-on-software-purchases).

See [perpetual versus subscription licensing](/blog/perpetual-versus-subscription-software-licensing) for the principles.

## Which Microsoft 365 plan, if you do choose the subscription

Moving off perpetual Office does not mean buying one plan for everybody. Three plans cover most Indian offices.

- **Business Basic** at {{price:microsoft-365-business-basic}} per user per year: web and mobile apps only, with email and Teams. Right for staff who do not need installed Office.
- **Business Standard** at {{price:microsoft-365-business-standard}}: adds installed applications. The usual replacement for a desk-based perpetual Office user.
- **Business Premium** at {{price:microsoft-365-business-premium}}: adds device management and security tooling for people who handle sensitive data or use personal phones for work.

The Business plans are capped at 300 seats in total, so firms growing past that need an Enterprise plan. Our [plan comparison](/blog/microsoft-365-business-basic-vs-standard-vs-premium) sets out the choice, and the [Standard versus Premium note](/blog/microsoft-365-business-standard-vs-business-premium) explains what the security layer adds.

## Questions to ask before you sign either way

For a perpetual licence:

- What is the supported end date of this exact edition, and what is our plan when it arrives?
- Which devices will it be installed on, and can the licence be moved if a machine is retired?
- Is the machine genuinely offline or fixed, or is that a habit we have never examined?

For a subscription:

- Who owns the list of assigned users, and who removes people who leave?
- Do we have seats that are assigned but never used? Our note on the [hidden cost of unused licences](/blog/hidden-cost-of-unused-software-licences) shows how common that is.
- Will we cross 300 users within two or three years?

## A decision rule you can write on one page

Choose LTSC when a device must stay frozen, offline or validated. Choose Home & Business 2024 when one or two people need the classic apps and nothing else. Choose Microsoft 365 for every person who works with mail, shared files and colleagues. Where an estate has more than one situation, license each separately and keep a register.

If you want the estate sized this way, [send us the device and user split](/enquiry) and we will quote it as a single estate. Prices on the site are tentative, exclude GST, and a written quotation fixes the final figure.

faqs.question: Is Office 2024 better than Microsoft 365 for business?
faqs.answer: Neither is better for everyone. Office LTSC 2024 suits fixed, offline or validated devices. Microsoft 365 suits people who need mail, shared files, Teams and continuous updates. Many companies need both, with the subscription for staff and LTSC for a few fixed machines.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Office LTSC and Office Home & Business 2024?
faqs.answer: LTSC is a volume-licensed, per-device business product that supports KMS or MAK activation. Home & Business 2024 is a one-time purchase for a single PC or Mac and does not support volume activation. Neither includes email hosting, OneDrive or Teams.

faqs.question: Does Office 2024 include Teams, email hosting or OneDrive?
faqs.answer: No. The perpetual editions install the desktop applications only. Business email on your own domain, Teams and 1 TB of OneDrive per user come with a Microsoft 365 Business subscription. Price those needs separately when comparing a perpetual licence with a subscription.

faqs.question: Which Microsoft 365 plan replaces perpetual Office for desk staff?
faqs.answer: Business Standard is the usual replacement, because it includes the installed Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook. Business Basic is web and mobile only, and Business Premium adds device management and security for people handling sensitive data.

faqs.question: How long should I compare costs over?
faqs.answer: Use the real replacement cycle of your hardware, often four to five years in Indian offices, and include the cost of the project needed to replace a perpetual licence at the end of its supported life. A one-year comparison favours the perpetual option unfairly.

faqs.question: Is there a seat limit on Microsoft 365 Business plans?
faqs.answer: Yes. The Business plans share a 300-seat cap per tenant across Basic, Standard and Premium combined. Companies approaching that size should ask for a quotation that includes the Enterprise plans.

needsVerification: Home & Business 2024 'one PC or Mac' and 'no volume activation' from catalogue; Publisher/Access in LTSC from catalogue. Nothing else beyond site facts. Hardware refresh cycle of four to five years is a general assumption.
